readings.section: The Architecture of the Covenant House
readings.title: Blueprint for the Physical Intersection
readings.subtitle: David establishes the material wealth required to construct the designated interface for YeHoVaH's presence.
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 29:1] And Daviḏ the sovereign said to all the assembly, “My son <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh, the <dn>את</dn> one whom <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen, is young and tender. And the work is great, because the palace is not for man but for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[2] “And with all <dn>My</dn> power <dn>I</dn> have prepared for the House of <dn>My</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>: <dn>את</dn> the gold for the gold, and <dn>את</dn> the silver for the silver, and <dn>את</dn> the bronze for the bronze, <dn>את</dn> the iron for the iron, and <dn>את</dn> the wood for the wood, <dn>את</dn> shoham stones, and <dn>את</dn> settings, and <dn>את</dn> fair stones of various colours, and <dn>את</dn> all kinds of precious stones, and <dn>את</dn> marble slabs – in large quantities.
[3] “And also, because <dn>I</dn> delighted in the House of <dn>My</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have treasure of gold and silver; <dn>I</dn> give for the House of <dn>My</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> even more than all that <dn>I</dn> have prepared for the Set-apart House:
[4] <dn>את</dn> three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and <dn>את</dn> seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the houses;
[5] the gold for the gold and the silver for the silver, and for all kinds of work to be done by the hands of craftsmen. Who then is moved to fill his hand today for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?”

readings.section: The Architecture of the Covenant House
readings.title: A Perfect Heart in the Divine Economy
readings.subtitle: The leaders of Yisra’ĕl align their terrestrial wealth with YeHoVaH's purpose, bringing functional harmony and joy.
readings.text:
[6] And the leaders of the fathers’ houses, and the leaders of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with the heads over the sovereign’s work, volunteered
[7] and gave for the work of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
[8] And those with whom were found precious stones gave <dn>את</dn> them to the treasury of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, into the hand of Yeḥi’ĕl the Gĕrshonite.
[9] And the people rejoiced, for they had given voluntarily, because with a perfect heart they had given voluntarily to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Daviḏ the sovereign also rejoiced greatly.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Covenant House
readings.title: The Blessing of Absolute Power
readings.subtitle: David publicly recognizes YeHoVaH as the singular, uncontained source of all greatness, wealth, and systemic authority.
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 29:10] And Daviḏ blessed <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before all the assembly. And Daviḏ said, “Blessed are <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, our Father, forever and ever.
[11] “<dn>Yours</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, is the greatness, the power and the comeliness, the pre-eminence and the excellency, because of all that is in the heavens and in the earth. <dn>Yours</dn> is the reign, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>You</dn> are exalted as head above all.
[12] “And the riches and the esteem come from <dn>Your</dn> presence, and <dn>You</dn> rule over all. And in <dn>Your</dn> hand is power and might, and in <dn>Your</dn> hand to make great and to give strength to all.
[13] “And now, our <dn>Elohim</dn>, we thank <dn>You</dn> and praise <dn>Your</dn> comely Name.
[14] “But who am <dn>I</dn>, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so voluntarily as this? For all comes from <dn>You</dn>, and we have given to <dn>You</dn> out of <dn>Your</dn> hand.
[15] “For we are sojourners and pilgrims before <dn>You</dn>, as were all our fathers; our days on earth are as a shadow, and without permanence.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Covenant House
readings.title: Guarding the Intent of the Heart
readings.subtitle: David petitions the Elohim of their fathers to anchor the minds of the people and grant Shelomoh the structural capacity to guard the Torah.
readings.text:
[16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, all this store that we have prepared to build <dn>You</dn> a house for <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Name is from <dn>Your</dn> hand, and all is of <dn>You</dn>.
[17] “And <dn>I</dn> know, <dn>My</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, that <dn>You</dn> are trying the heart and desire uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart <dn>I</dn> have voluntarily given all these. And now with joy <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>Your</dn> people, who are present here to give voluntarily to <dn>You</dn>.
[18] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yisra’ĕl, our fathers, guard <dn>את</dn> this forever in the intent of the thoughts of the heart of <dn>Your</dn> people, and prepare <dn>את</dn> their heart toward <dn>You</dn>.
[19] “And give my son Shelomoh a perfect heart to guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> commands and <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> witnesses and <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> laws, to do all, and to build the palace for which <dn>I</dn> have prepared.”
[20] And Daviḏ said to all the assembly, “Now bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.” And all the assembly blessed <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, and bowed their heads and did obeisance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the sovereign.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Covenant House
readings.title: Ascending Offerings and the Second Anointing
readings.subtitle: The nation seals the covenant transition with an abundance of sacrifices, confirming Shelomoh as the appointed leader.
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 29:21] And they slaughtered slaughterings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and offered ascending offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the next day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and slaughterings in large numbers for all Yisra’ĕl.
[22] And they ate and drank before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with great joy on that day. And they set up <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh son of Daviḏ to reign the second time, and anointed him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to be leader, and <dn>את</dn> Tsaḏoq to be priest.

readings.title: The Vulnerability of Flesh
readings.subtitle: The physical decline of Sovereign David initiates a critical vulnerability in the hierarchy of Yisra’ĕl.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 1:1] And Sovereign Daviḏ was old, advanced in years. And they covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.
[2] So his servants said to him, “Let them seek for our master the sovereign a young woman, a maiden, and she shall stand before the sovereign and be his companion, and shall lie in your bosom, so that our master the sovereign gets warm.”
[3] And they sought for a beautiful young woman in all the border of Yisra’ĕl, and found <dn>את</dn> Aḇishaġ the Shunammite, and brought <dn>את</dn> her to the sovereign.
[4] And the young woman was very beautiful. And she was a companion for the sovereign, and served him, but the sovereign did not know her.

readings.title: Adoniyahu's Unlawful Exaltation
readings.subtitle: Operating in the spirit of the adversary, Adoniyahu attempts to usurp the designated throne through self-appointment and exclusion.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 1:5] And Aḏoniyah son of Ḥaggith exalted himself, saying, “<dn>I</dn> reign.” And he prepared for himself a chariot and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
[6] Now his father had not worried him at any time by saying, “Why have you done so?” He was also very good-looking. And he was born after Aḇshalom.
[7] And he talked with <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah and with <dn>את</dn> Eḇyathar the priest, and they supported Aḏoniyah.
[8] But Tsaḏoq the priest, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and Nathan the prophet, and Shim‛i, and Rĕ‛i, and the mighty men who belonged to Daviḏ were not with Aḏoniyahu.
[9] And Aḏoniyahu slaughtered sheep and cattle and fatlings by the stone of Zoḥeleth, which is by Ên Roġĕl. He also invited all his brothers, the sovereign’s sons, and all the men of Yehuḏah, servants of the sovereign.
[10] But he did not invite <dn>את</dn> Nathan the prophet, or <dn>את</dn> Benayahu, or <dn>את</dn> the mighty men, or <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh his brother.

readings.title: Nathan's Strategic Counsel
readings.subtitle: The prophet orchestrates a precise counter-measure to secure the life of the true heir and maintain the divine decree.
readings.text:
[11] Nathan then spoke to Bathsheḇa the mother of Shelomoh, saying, “Have you not heard that Aḏoniyahu son of Ḥaggith has become sovereign, and Daviḏ our master does not know it?
[12] “And now, come let me give you advice, and deliver <dn>את</dn> your own life and <dn>את</dn> the life of your son Shelomoh.
[13] “Go immediately to Sovereign Daviḏ and say to him, ‘Did you not, my master, O sovereign, swear to your female servant, saying, “Certainly, your son Shelomoh shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne”? Why then has Aḏoniyahu become sovereign?’
[14] “Look, while you are still speaking there with the sovereign let me come in after you and confirm your words.”

readings.title: Bathsheba Invokes the Covenant Promise
readings.subtitle: Bathsheba confronts the failing king, calling upon his binding oath to YeHoVaH to establish Shelomoh's terrestrial authority.
readings.text:
[15] And Bathsheḇa went into the room to the sovereign. Now the sovereign was very old, and Aḇishaġ the Shunammite was serving the sovereign.
[16] And Bathsheḇa bowed and did obeisance to the sovereign. And the sovereign said, “What do you wish?”
[17] And she said to him, “My master, you swore by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> to your female servant, saying, ‘Certainly, Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’
[18] “And now, look! Aḏoniyah has become sovereign. And now, my master the sovereign, you do not know about it.
[19] “And he has slaughtered great numbers of bulls and fatlings and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the sovereign, and Eḇyathar the priest, and Yo’aḇ the commander of the army, but he did not invite <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh your servant.
[20] “And you my master, O sovereign, the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl are on you, to declare to them who is going to sit on the throne of my master the sovereign after him.
[21] “Otherwise it shall be, when my master the sovereign rests with his fathers, that <dn>I</dn> and my son Shelomoh shall be considered sinners.”

readings.title: The Prophet Demands a Verdict
readings.subtitle: Nathan verifies the systemic threat to the throne, demanding David clarify the official lineage of command.
readings.text:
[22] And see, while she was still speaking with the sovereign, Nathan the prophet also came in.
[23] So they informed the sovereign, saying, “Here is Nathan the prophet.” And when he came in before the sovereign, he bowed down before the sovereign with his face to the ground.
[24] And Nathan said, “My master, O sovereign, have you said, ‘Aḏoniyahu shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne’?
[25] “For he has gone down today, and has slaughtered great numbers of bulls and fatlings and sheep, and has invited all the sovereign’s sons, and the commanders of the army, and Eḇyathar the priest. And look! They are eating and drinking before him. And they say, ‘Let Sovereign Aḏoniyahu live!’
[26] “But he has not invited <dn>את</dn> me, me your servant, nor <dn>את</dn> Tsaḏoq the priest, nor <dn>את</dn> Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, nor <dn>את</dn> your servant Shelomoh.
[27] “If this matter is from my master the sovereign, then you did not let your servant know who should sit on the throne of my master the sovereign after him.”

readings.subsection: The Decree of the Appointed Heir
readings.title: The Oath of Ransomed Life
readings.subtitle: David invokes the Name of the Creator who delivered him, cementing the legal transfer of power to Shelomoh.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 1:28] And Sovereign Daviḏ answered and said, “Call Bathsheḇa to me.” So she came into the sovereign’s presence and stood before the sovereign.
[29] And the sovereign took an oath and said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who has ransomed <dn>את</dn> my life out of all distress,
[30] even as <dn>I</dn> swore to you by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Certainly, Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,’ even so <dn>I</dn> do this day.”
[31] And Bathsheḇa bowed with her face to the earth, and did obeisance to the sovereign, and said, “Let my master Sovereign Daviḏ live forever!”

readings.title: The Horn of Oil and the Shophar
readings.subtitle: Shelomoh is officially designated as the authorized ruler at Giḥon, sparking an earth-shattering celebration of order restored.
readings.text:
[32] And Sovereign Daviḏ said, “Call me Tsaḏoq the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa.” And they came before the sovereign.
[33] And the sovereign said to them, “Take with <dn>את</dn> you <dn>את</dn> the servants of your master, and you shall have <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh my son ride on my own mule, and take <dn>את</dn> him down to Giḥon.
[34] “And there Tsaḏoq the priest and Nathan the prophet shall anoint <dn>את</dn> him sovereign over Yisra’ĕl. And blow the shophar, and say, ‘Let Sovereign Shelomoh live!’
[35] “And you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, and he shall reign in my place. For <dn>I</dn> have commanded him to be ruler over Yisra’ĕl and over Yehuḏah.”
[36] And Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa answered the sovereign and said, “Amĕn! So says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of my master the sovereign.
[37] “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has been with my master the sovereign, so let <dn>Him</dn> be with Shelomoh and make his throne greater than the throne of my master Sovereign Daviḏ.”
[38] Then Tsaḏoq the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and the Kerĕthites, and the Pelĕthites went down and had <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh ride on Sovereign Daviḏ’s mule, and took <dn>את</dn> him to Giḥon.
[39] And Tsaḏoq the priest took <dn>את</dn> a horn of oil from the Tent and anointed <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh. And they blew with the shophar, and all the people said, “Let Sovereign Shelomoh live!”
[40] And all the people came up after him. And the people played the flutes and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth was split by their noise!

readings.subsection: The Collapse of the Usurper's Reign
readings.title: The Disruption of the Adversarial Feast
readings.subtitle: The undeniable sound of the true king's ascension shatters Adoniyahu's illusion of power, scattering his conspirators.
readings.text:
[41] And Aḏoniyahu and all the guests who were with him heard it as they had finished eating. And Yo’aḇ heard the voice of the shophar, and said, “Why is the city in such a noisy uproar?”
[42] And he was still speaking, then see, Yonathan came, son of Eḇyathar the priest. And Aḏoniyahu said to him, “Come in, for you are a brave man, and you bring good news.”
[43] But Yonathan answered and said to Aḏoniyahu, “No! Our master Sovereign Daviḏ has made Shelomoh sovereign,
[44] and the sovereign has sent with him Tsaḏoq the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and the Kerĕthites, and the Pelĕthites. And they had him ride on the sovereign’s mule.
[45] “And Tsaḏoq the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him sovereign at Giḥon. And they have gone up from there rejoicing, and the city is moved. This is the noise you heard.
[46] “And further, Shelomoh sits on the throne of the reign.
[47] “And further, the servants of the sovereign have gone to bless our master Sovereign Daviḏ, saying, ‘Let your <dn>Elohim</dn> make <dn>את</dn> the name of Shelomoh better than your name, and <dn>את</dn> his throne greater than your throne.’ And the sovereign bowed himself on the bed.
[48] “And the sovereign also said thus, ‘Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, who has given one to sit on my throne this day, while my eyes see it!’ ”
[49] And all the guests who were invited by Aḏoniyahu were afraid, and rose, and each one went his way.

readings.subsection: The Prerogative of the True King
readings.title: Conditional Mercy at the Slaughter-Place
readings.subtitle: Shelomoh exercises the authority of the throne, granting life to his rival contingent upon his functional righteousness.
readings.text:
[50] And Aḏoniyahu was afraid of Shelomoh, and rose, and went and took hold of the horns of the slaughter-place.
[51] And it was reported to Shelomoh, saying, “Look, Aḏoniyahu is afraid of Sovereign Shelomoh. And look, he has taken hold of the horns of the slaughter-place, saying, ‘Let Sovereign Shelomoh swear to me today that he does not put <dn>את</dn> his servant to death with the sword.’ ”
[52] And Shelomoh said, “If he proves himself a worthy man, not one hair of him is going to fall to the earth, but if evil is found in him, then he shall die.”
[53] And Sovereign Shelomoh sent, and they brought him down from the slaughter-place. And he came and fell down before Sovereign Shelomoh. And Shelomoh said to him, “Go to your house.”
